text.p: Belgian temporary employment company Creyf's NV said on Thursday it was cautious about 1997 profit due to a price war in the sector.
"We are very restrained (in our outlook)," Creyf's chief executive officer and chairman Michel Van Hemele told a news conference. "Nobody knows to where the price war will lead."
He said the market had held steady for a number of months from the start of the summer of 1996, but that the price war had been heating up again since from the start of 1997.
He said, however, that demand for temporary employment had increased at the start of this year.
"January was good but February even better and March will certainly be just as good as February," Van Hemele said.
Creyf's had 1996 group net profit of 143 million francs against 141 million francs the year before.
